text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
IZVESTIA
- Relations between Russia and Belarus have worsened as President Boris Yeltsin expressed his indignation over the arrest by Belarussian authorities of a Russian television crew.
- Debate on the auction of Svyazinvest shares is growing into a major row among Russia's leading financial groups.
- A deal on selling 55 Russian Sukhoi Su-27 fighters to China is expected to be signed by the end of the year.
- Russia's leading confectionery maker Red October plans to raise about $65 million in the near future, says the paper.

- The new crew which will leave for the Mir space station in two weeks expressed confidence they could repair damage caused by a serious accident last month. The 11-year-old Mir will be in use till 2000, a Russian space official is quoted as saying.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- Official signing of the Svyazinvest deal does not mean that the banking war is over, the paper says.
- Winners of the Svyazinvest sell-off say they plan to invest in the company and its regional affiliated companies.
- A new tax on currency purchases has caused chaos in exchange offices across the country.
- President Boris Yeltsin threatens to revise the treaty with Belarus if Minsk's conflict with Russian journalists is not resolved.
- Russia's central bank is planning to raise 30 trillion roubles by selling OFZ government interest-bearing bonds. The sale starts today.
SEVODNYA
- The mandate of Russian peacekeepers in Georgia's breakaway Abkhazia region expires today, but the future of the Russian 1,500 contingent is not yet decided.
- The head of Russia's tax service, Alexander Pochinok, promised to crack down on big tax defaulters.
- The paper is critically looking into the activity of U.S. financier George Soros, who invested in a consortium that has just acquired a quarter of Svyazinvest.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- Russian peacekeepers are likely to prolong their stay in Abkhazia, but as of August 1 they will not have a clear legal status.
- President Yeltsin put an end to the conflict over Svyazinvest.
ROSSIISKIYE VESTI
- The number of Russian students choosing economics as a subject has grown by 94.5 percent in the last 10 years
SOVIETSKAYA ROSSIA
- The opposition should take power in Russia and change the course of reforms in the country, the paper's expert says.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin is said to have ordered the government to study the results of the auction of Svyazinvest shares.
- The paper reports on a Swiss newspaper story alleging a top Kremlin security official avoided taxes.
-- Svetlana Kovaleva, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
